### rule_compute_equivalence
- Mechanical sweep (scratch): every `compute_basis` quote of P1–P5 is verbatim in its own rule (XF 4 PASS); every `baseline.rule` is verbatim in the rule; every factor binding names a compute line; factor binding sets are pairwise disjoint in every policy.
- Rounding (XF 6): P1/P3 `int(MX(0,…))` = "a whole number of days … never below zero" (all addends integers) — match. P2/P4/P5 `RND(MX(0,…),2)` once at the end = "never below zero and is rounded to the cent, half up, once at the end" — placement matches. Observation O-G1: the DSL `RND` is Python `round` (binary float, half-to-even), not half up; only bites on an exact half cent (P4 posting-basis tier 1 can produce arbitrary fractions). Inner roundings: P2 tier 2 ceil(std/2) "rounded up to the next whole dollar" = compute; P4 tier 2 int(std/2) "rounded down to the whole dollar" = compute; P5 tier 2 ceil(3·std/4) = compute.
- Windows: `within_months=12/3` in the DSL keeps rows with 0 <= MONTHS(row_date, today) < N, MONTHS counting a month only once its day of month is reached — matches "(a month counts once its day of the month is reached)"; the anniversary-day row (MONTHS = N) is excluded by compute while the words "within the twelve whole months before" do not say whether the N-th anniversary day is inside (XF 8 boundary wording; observation O-G2 unless a seed row sits on it — checked per task).
- **F-G1 (P3 rule vs compute, XF 11)**: the rule selects ONE change — "The removal or exclusion is the auto_driver_removed or auto_driver_excluded change on the backing term whose driver_name is exactly the certificate's filed_driver_name and, when several are recorded, the one with the latest change_effective_date." — and prices the counting, the relationship and the points from "that removal or exclusion change". Compute instead gives any removal priority regardless of date: `counted_days: … if removed_on else (… if (excluded_on and term_end) …)`, `points: XLATEST(…auto_driver_removed…) if removed_on else XLATEST(…auto_driver_excluded…)`, `relation: XLATEST(removed…) or XLATEST(excluded…)`; the factor ladder also says "no removal but an exclusion". Same situation, two conclusions: removal 2026-09-01, later exclusion 2026-09-20 of the same filed driver, SR-26 on 2026-10-07, term expiring 2027-03-01, std 10: rule (latest = exclusion) -> MN(10, 145) = 10 run-off days; compute (removal first) -> MX(0, 10 − 36) = 0. Also the same-day tie among several removals/exclusions is unstated (XLATEST keeps the first row in dict order) — XF 8 member.
- Ladder-tier vs rule-tier: every `factors[].ladder` tier is a sentence of its rule and a branch of its `decides` expression, and vice versa (checked for all 28 factors).
- No empty promises found in P1, P2, P4, P5 beyond F-G1.

### prerequisite_sentences
- P2: "The refiling fee is fixed only after the replaced certificate carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date." — connective "only after"; record state (sr26_date, certificate_end_date of the replaced filing); no tool/id/snake_case. Writers that set those fields: transmit_lapse_sr26 (P1) and transmit_removal_sr26 (P3); the replaced certificate of P2 is by scope an Operator certificate on a Named Non-Owner term, which only P1's rule covers ("Operator certificate … because its Named Non-Owner backing term was cancelled"), P3's rule being for Owner certificates — one reading. Derivation: replaced Operator filing is `filed`, its NNO term reinstated with lapse -> P1's rule says such a certificate receives a policy_cancelled SR-26 -> transmit it -> fields set -> P2 priced. PASS.
- P5 edge 1: "The household certificate fee is not fixed until a certificate it is read against whose filed driver has been removed from the backing term carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date." — "not … until"; state; only P3's rule SR-26s an Owner certificate for a removed driver. PASS.
- P5 edge 2: "The household certificate fee is fixed only after the certificate it is read against shows a filing fee charge for its own request." — "only after"; state (an fee_assessed row on that filing); only P4 posts a fee on an existing filing (P2/P5 book fees on new filings). PASS.
- **F-G5 (P4 sentence broader than its condition)**: "A late-posted filing fee is not fixed until **a certificate** whose filed driver has been removed from its backing term carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date." The condition is "When **the filing's** filed driver has an auto_driver_removed change on the backing term, **its** fr_filings row carries …". The sentence names any certificate whose driver was removed; the condition names only the filing being priced. Second reading in the same situation: customer with filing A (fee unposted, driver not removed) and filing B (driver removed, still `filed`): sentence -> the fee on A waits on B's SR-26; condition -> A's fee is fixed now (standing tier 0, no wait). Per-task consequence in 1.md.
- Docstrings silent about sequence; the depended-on rules (P1, P3, P4) do not restate any of these sentences. P1 and P3 name each other's case as "the removal rule"/"the lapse rule" in scope carve-outs — not a dependency, no edge needed (observation O-G3, no order is stated).

Parameter labels honest (every parameter tier substitutes a number). No two tiers of one ladder select the same value (all ladders checked: distinct K values or 0 only on the fall-through).

Scope test of fall-through tiers (XF 9 / "holds of every customer who reaches this write"):
- **F-G7 P2 continuity_charge**: tiers 1 and 2 both require "the replaced certificate carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date"; the fall-through ("otherwise no continuity charge") is the no-SR-26 case. P2's scope is a certificate that "has received an SR-26", P2's own prerequisite sentence fixes the fee "only after the replaced certificate carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date", and base fr_agg_multi_holding allows a reinstatement_refiling only while the earlier filing is cancellation_filed. The condition part "carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date" holds of every customer who reaches this write; the fall-through — which is also the factor's `baseline` (0) — is unreachable in scope: the in-scope ladder has 2 tiers.
- **F-G8 P3 removal_counting**: fall-through "With no such removal or exclusion recorded, the standard removal run-off is counted from the SR-26 date"; P3's scope is an SR-26 "because its filed driver was removed from, or excluded on, the … backing term" (reason filer_excluded_or_removed). Every customer reaching this write has a removal or exclusion: in-scope ladder 2 tiers, and the factor's baseline (std) is the out-of-scope tier. (Its `baseline` equals the policy baseline, so the baseline-honesty test passes; the ladder test fails.)
- P1, P4, P5 fall-throughs are in scope.

Realism (hard criterion, XF 16 and the "unreal ladder" test). The quantities are (a) the SR-26 run-off — the days after the SR-26 until the state stops treating the driver as certified, which state financial-responsibility practice ties to the state's cancellation-notice period and the form, and which the carrier fixes uniformly (the base: certificate_runoff_days 10 for every form and state); and (b) a flat administrative SR-22/FR-44 filing fee charged per request (base: 25 / 35 by form, free for corrected_refiling). Conditions and outcomes no nonstandard auto carrier weighs for these quantities — **F-G9, each a member**:
- P1 `clean_payment_notice`: payments received / returned payments on any billing plan in 12 months lengthen how long a cancelled driver stays certified — no carrier or state extends third-party certification for good payers on a lapsed driver (it would lengthen the carrier's own exposure on an unpaid risk).
- P1 `lapse_history_notice`: one prior NNO reinstatement fee +3 days, two or more +1, none 0 — lapse count is an underwriting variable, not a notice-period variable, and the non-monotone schedule rewards one lapse over none.
- P1 `term_remaining_notice`: days from the SR-26 date to the expiration of a term that is already cancelled — a cancelled term's former expiration has no bearing on the certificate's end.
- P1 `dui_requirement_notice`: the form split (FR-44 vs SR-22) is a real distinction, but the tier condition "more than 365 days left to required_through_date" is not weighed by any state or carrier for the SR-26 run-off (and the base says the company "never computes the requirement period").
- P2 `lapse_length_charge`, `delinquency_charge` (count of NNO nonpayment notices), `requirement_charge` (days to required_through_date): lapse and delinquency are priced in the Non-Owner premium/reinstatement fee, not in the per-form filing fee; the remaining requirement period does not change the cost of filing a form.
- P2 `data_recheck`: charges $5/$10 for a prior data/limits rejection, while the charter's own fee schedule makes data correction free (`fee_free_filing_reasons: [corrected_refiling]`) — a carrier publishing that schedule would not re-charge it on the refiling.
- P3 `household_relationship_notice` (spouse +5, relative +3), `certificate_use_notice` (copies issued in 3 months; copies are free and are not use of coverage), `driver_record_notice` (0–3 points +2, 4–8 +1, more 0): none is weighed for when a removed driver stops being certified; points-based more-notice-for-cleaner-drivers is trivia.
- P4 `plan_settlement_credit` (plan status), `acceptance_credit` (days the STATE took to accept — outside the carrier's control and not a fee input), `driver_listing_credit` (removal $0.50 / exclusion $0.25), `copy_issued_credit` (more free copies issued -> bigger credit): trivia keyed credits on a flat fee.
- P5 `schedule_change_charge` (any driver's recent removal/exclusion surcharges another driver's filing fee), `plan_balance_adjustment` (±$1 by plan balance sign).
Borderline, recorded as observations O-G7 (plausible company schedules): P1 runoff_counting (holding the certificate through an open reinstatement window; counting from the lapse start), P2 refiling_fee_basis (credit for a recent fee), P2 continuity_charge (credit/re-certification charge — realism fine, scope F-G7), P3 removal_counting, P4 posting_basis_method (O-G5 tension), P4 certificate_standing_credit, P5 household_fee_basis, household_standing_credit, joint_fee_credit (double-credits the same standing fee already netted in the basis), continuous_coverage_credit (loyalty-flavoured).

Surviving factor counts after F-G7/F-G8/F-G9: P1 1 (runoff_counting, method; 0 parameter) — **below 4 and below 2 parameter**; P2 1 (refiling_fee_basis) — below 4; P3 0 — below 4 and no method; P4 2 (posting_basis_method, certificate_standing_credit) — below 4; P5 4 (household_fee_basis method; household_standing_credit, joint_fee_credit, continuous_coverage_credit parameter) — meets bounds. **F-G10**: P1–P4 fail the 4–6 / 2-parameter / 1-method bounds counting only surviving rules.

Multi-source / cross-difficulty availability per task scope: {P1,P2}: clean_payment_notice (returned vs received payment rows) multi-source but struck (F-G9); among survivors runoff_counting tiers read one NNO row + its variant — not multi-source; refiling_fee_basis T1/T2 read fee rows + the latest fee row of one ledger. {P3,P4,P5}: survivors household_fee_basis T2 (read-against filing date AND backing auto term expiration — two records) multi-source; cross-difficulty survivors: household_fee_basis (auto), continuous_coverage_credit (nonowner). Per-task confirmation in task files.

- **F2-D1 (XF 19 deadlock / XF 20 zero-amount edge)**: P5 waits for a fee standing above zero on the replaced certificate; P4 is the only write that can bring it about, and (a) P4's figure is 0.00 on reachable worlds — e.g. delay > 180 (posting basis 0) on an AZ-garaged AZ filing, Paid-in-Full plan, 250/500/100 package, SR-26 in run-off: MX(0, 0 − 2 + 0 − 5 + 0 + 0) = 0.00; the tool accepts "a non-negative amount", the 0.00 row leaves fees standing at 0, P5 never becomes fixed; (b) P4's own words say no fee is charged again after 180 days (F2-P1), so a faithful agent posts nothing and P5 waits forever; (c) a replaced certificate requested with filing_reason corrected_refiling carries no fee by base ("No fee is charged for a corrected_refiling") and is outside P4's scope (fee_charged_filing_reasons only) — no write in the charter can ever make P5's edge hold, so a mover whose certificate is a corrected refiling can never be refiled. Three members.
- No cross-problem order stated in any rule outside the declared edges ("priced under their own rules" / "takes its run-off from the owner-term rule" are scope carve-outs).

### findings (r4), each class listed exhaustively
- **F4-1 (XF 23/25 "each dimension once")**: certificate type and backing type are charged as two factors, but in this charter the backing type is fixed by the certificate type (variants: SR-22/FR-44 Operator -> backing_policy_category nonowner; Owner and Owner-Operator -> auto; base: "operator when the backing is the filer's Named Non-Owner Policy"). Every Operator certificate takes both the operator tier and the NNO tier, every Owner/Owner-Operator certificate both its type tier and the owner tier — one partition charged twice. Members (4 pairs): P1 lapse_type_notice + lapse_backing_notice; P2 refiling_type_charge + refiling_backing_charge; P3 cancel_type_notice + cancel_backing_notice; P4 recharge_type_charge + recharge_backing_charge. (P5 carries type only — not a member.)
- **F4-2 (XF 9, fall-through out of scope)**: the backing ladders' fall-through "no backing term on record" cannot occur — every SR-26, refiling and re-charge in scope rests on a backing term on record. In-scope ladder 2 tiers. Members: P1 lapse_backing_notice, P2 refiling_backing_charge, P3 cancel_backing_notice, P4 recharge_backing_charge.
- **F4-3 (XF 9 / "a condition that holds of every customer who reaches this write")**: P1 lapse_runoff_counting tiers "cancelled at the insured_request and carries a reinstatement_date" and "any other cancellation_reason" are unreachable: P1's scope is a term reinstated with a lapse, and both charters allow reinstatement only after nonpayment (auto.yaml / nonowner.yaml eligibility nonpayment_only: "Only a term whose cancellation_reason is nonpayment can be reinstated."). The method factor has one reachable tier; its baseline tier is out of scope.
- **F4-4 (XF 9, regression of the revision_1 F-G7 class)**: P2 refiling_fee_method fall-through "Otherwise, including a replaced certificate with no SR-26 date, … the standard refiling fee" is out of scope — P2's scope is a certificate that "has received an SR-26", its own sentence fixes the fee "only after the replaced certificate carries an SR-26 date and a certificate end date", and base fr_agg_multi_holding allows a reinstatement_refiling only while the earlier filing is cancellation_filed. In-scope ladder 2 tiers; the declared edge effect ("moves from the standard refiling fee to half of it") moves out of that unreachable tier.
- **F4-5 (XF 24/25 incidental key)**: P5 transfer_fee_method keys its tiers on "whether a filing fee stands on it (its fee charges less its fee reversals above zero)" — a ledger aggregate, not one of point 24's only acceptable keys (state, form and type, backing type, channel, how coverage ended); point 25 names ledger keys as padding. Member: P5 transfer_fee_method (its other condition, certification standing, is acceptable). It is also the key that carries the P5<-P4 edge.
- **F4-6 (XF 5c, sibling overwrites)**: P1 and P3 both retire the base sentence "An SR-26 is transmitted no later than sr26_transmit_within_days calendar days after the date coverage under the backing term ended." P3's replaced_by reads "…counted from the closed_date as day 0; a cancellation SR-26 not transmitted by then is still owed…", without excluding the lapse SR-26 (whose closed_date the reinstatement clears); P1's reads "…calendar days being counted from that date as day 0; a lapse SR-26 not transmitted by then is still owed…", without naming the cancellation case. For a lapse SR-26 the in-force text gives day 0 = closed_date (P3) and day 0 = lapse_start_date (P1). No scored consequence in either world (the late clause makes the SR-26 owed either way and the run-off counts from the actual transmission).
- Observation O4-1: P4 keys both its method (the filing's certification standing) and its ending charge (the backing term's cancellation_reason) on "how coverage ended" in the rule's own words; they read different records and differ in value, so not counted as a member. O4-2: P1/P3 form ladders key on the term's financial_responsibility_filing stamp (honest source per XF 18); "recorded as backing none" while backing a certificate is an inconsistent but not impossible record. O4-3: state group (backing state) plus out-of-state (filing vs backing) both read the backing state — point 25 lists them as separate publishable keys, so accepted (contrast revision_2 F2-R3, judged before point 25).
- Realism otherwise: every remaining key is a point-24/25 publishable key (state schedule groups, form, type, backing, filing vs backing state, how coverage ended or was restored); three-tier groupings as allowed by point 25. XF 26: no recorded amount embeds any factor.
- Surviving factors after F4-1 (one of each pair kept), F4-2/F4-3/F4-4 (ladders failing scope struck), F4-5: P1 4 parameters, **no method** (counting struck); P2 3 parameters, **no method**; P3 5 (method + 4); P4 5 (method + 4); P5 3 parameters, **no method**. **F4-7 (bounds)**: P1, P2, P5 lack a surviving method factor (P2 and P5 also fall below 4).
